title: Choose the visual world for Park Patrol
question: The roll assigned Computation Pad. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All options stay white-first with green, as you asked.

options.label: Computation Pad
options.lineage: Engineering computation pads every DLSL engineering student has filled in
options.thesis: Live parking measured on a precise green survey grid, like a startup's engineering notebook.
options.viewport: Slim white top bar; left column has one huge free-spot numeral with a live 2s pulse and a ruled meter; right side shows the lot plan drawn on a faint green 24px grid.
options.risk: If the grid is overdone it turns into graph-paper costume; it has to stay faint and only sit under the map and meters.

raised.raise: Map geometry snaps to a strict 24px module, and spot labels stay one fixed size at every zoom.
One numeral owns the hero; everything around it stays small and quiet.
Compressed type scale: weight and color carry rank, with three sizes outside the hero numeral.
A spot looks the same in the map, the list, and the sheet: same scale, same ground.
The spot list reflows in whole cells and never squeezes a tile.

options.label: Bay Indicator
options.lineage: Mall smart-parking lights above each bay and the 'AVAILABLE 23' entrance sign
options.thesis: Every spot is a light: green for open, quiet for taken, exactly like the mall lots Filipinos know.
options.viewport: A big entrance-sign style count in a white panel with a lit green digit, then a row of 18 indicator lights you can scan in one glance above the map.
options.risk: The most familiar route: close to what most smart-parking dashboards already do.

options.label: Arrivals Board
options.lineage: Split-flap concourse departure boards, translated onto white
options.thesis: The lot as a live arrivals board: every spot is a row that flips when its status changes.
options.viewport: Big count up top, then a board of A1 to A18 rows with status and 'since' columns; changes flip one character at a time.
options.case: Great for the admin activity feed and status changes; the guest page loses the spatial lot map, so it only holds the clarity axis.
options.risk: Flipping cells can feel gimmicky if they animate too often.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: The lot drawn as a transit diagram.
options.viewport: The lot as a line diagram.
options.risk: A midnight ground breaks your white brief.
options.case: Loses both axes: an 18-spot lot has no routes.
options.kept: Strict geometry module and fixed-size labels on the map.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything as a coded catalog entry.
options.viewport: One plot on a black field.
options.case: Loses both axes: guests need plain words.
options.kept: One element owns the field: the free-spot numeral.

options.label: Timetable Rack
options.thesis: One type size, rank by weight.
options.viewport: Raked slides on a lit bed.
options.risk: The goldenrod ground breaks the white brief.
options.case: Loses both axes: raked panels fight the map.
options.kept: Compressed type scale where weight carries rank.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.risk: Cream and serif is the AI-slop default.
options.kept: Same scale and ground for a spot everywhere it appears.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: A ranked roster of rounded cells.
options.risk: Too toy-like for a security console.
options.kept: Whole-cell reflow in the spot list.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A standard white SaaS dashboard with a green accent, done really well.
canonCard.viewport: KPI tiles across the top, then a map card and a table card.
canonCard.risk: Polished, but hard to tell apart from every other dashboard.
